title: Protocol for Evaluating Neuronal Polarity in Murine Models
protocol: Isolate E18.5 rat embryos.
Dissect the hippocampus from isolated rat embryos.
Digest the dissected hippocampi using enzymatic solutions.
Plate the digested neurons onto culture dishes for further analysis.
Place E18.5 pregnant rat inside the CO2 euthanasia chamber for rodents.
Open the CO2 flux until a reduction in breath frequency is noticed and the rat is completely asleep (usually 8-10 seconds).
Proceed with cervical dislocation once vital signs are no longer detectable.
Sterilize the belly zone with 70% v/v ethanol.
Make an incision in the middle zone of the belly to expose embryos.
Transfer embryos to a 100 mm petri dish partially filled with pre-chilled PBS (4°C).
Check the pregnancy and size of embryos (total length should be close to 1.5-1.8 cm).
Open embryo sacs with a small scissor.
Transfer each embryo to a new 100 mm petri dish partially filled with pre-chilled PBS (4°C).
Isolate heads by making an incision at the neck using a small scissor.
Open the skull using a micro-scissor, cutting the dorsal line of the head from the neck to the front.
Hold heads by introducing a fine tweezer through the eye sockets.
Transfer the embryonic brains to a 60 mm petri dish previously filled with 3–4 mL HBSS supplemented with 0.35 g/L NaHCO3.
Under scope, split hemispheres with a tweezer.
Remove and discard meninges from each hemisphere using a fine tweezer (No.5).
Isolate the hippocampus using a micro-scissor.
Transfer isolated hippocampi to a new 60 mm petri dish pre-filled with 4.5 mL HBSS.
If needed, transfer cerebral cortices to a petri dish pre-filled with 4.0 mL HBSS.
Add 0.5 mL of 10× trypsin to the petri dish containing hippocampi (pre-filled with 4.5 mL HBSS).
Incubate the mixture 20 min at 37°C.
Transfer digested hippocampi to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Make three quick washes with 2 mL HBSS.
Discard HBSS and add 2–3 mL of 10% HS MEM pre-warmed at 37°C.
Resuspend hippocampi with a glass Pasteur pipette using up-and-down movements until obtaining a homogenous suspension.
Repeat the resuspension procedure with a “half-diameter tip” pipette.
Finally, repeat the up-and-down movements using a “quarter-diameter tip” pipette until homogenate is achieved.
Avoid making foam during the process.
Add 0.5 mL of 10× trypsin and 0.5 mL of 10× DNase to the petri dish containing cortices, which are pre-filled with 4.0 mL HBSS.
Incubate the mixture for 25 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer the cortices to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Perform three quick washes using 4–5 mL of HBSS.
Discard the HBSS and replace it with 5 mL of pre-warmed (at 37°C) 10% HS MEM.
Repeat several “up and down” movements using a 1,000 μL micropipette to obtain a homogeneous suspension of cells.
Avoid making foam during pipetting.
Dilute cells 1/100 for counting.
Count cells using a Neubauer chamber.
Estimate the yield [cells / (μL or mL)].
If cortices are resuspended in 5 mL 10% HS MEM, expect a yield close to 10^7 neurons/mL.
Isolate cells after digestion; presence of clumps indicates inefficient enzymatic/mechanical digestion.
Repeat mechanical digestion until isolated cells are obtained or check trypsin efficiency.
Estimate the volume needed to plate neurons at the required density based on table:files/protocols_protocol_190_2.csv.
Plate hippocampal or cortical neurons in pre-coated PLL culture dishes using 10% HS MEM.
Replace 10% HS MEM with Neurobasal medium supplemented with B27, Glutamax and Pen/Strep once neurons are attached (1–2 h after plating).
Change the culture medium every 3–4 days, preserving 1/3 of the volume.
Prepare a fresh solution of 4% w/v paraformaldehyde (PFA) and 4% w/v sucrose, dissolved in PBS.
Adjust pH to 7.4.
Fix neurons with 4% PFA/sucrose solution for 20 min at room temperature.
Wash neurons with PBS for immunofluorescence staining.
Stain neurons, neurites, and growth cones by immunofluorescence (IF) using tubulin (ß3-tubulin or Tyr-tubulin) antibody and phalloidin.
Stain neurons with tubulin (ß3-tubulin or Tyr-tubulin) antibody and phalloidin.
Visualize minor neurites and axons by immunofluorescence.
Stain neurons with MAP2 and Tau-1 antibodies.
Identify somatodendritic and axonal compartments.
Stain neurons with synapsin and MAP2 antibodies.
Visualize dendrites and branching at this stage by immunofluorescence.
Stain neurons with PSD-95 and synaptophysin to visualize post and pre-synaptic terminals.
Alternatively, stain with MAP2 and AnkG antibodies.
Detect dendrites and the assembly of the axon initial segment (AIS) of mature axons.
Anesthetize the animal.
Sterilize the surgical area.
Place the pregnant mouse inside the chamber containing the isoflurane + oxygen mix for anesthesia.
Increase the isoflurane flow to 4% to achieve full anesthesia quickly (visible by reduced breath frequency).
Transfer the animal to a warming system at 37°C and adjust the isoflurane flow to 2%-2.5% for surgery maintenance.
Pinch the toes with tweezers to confirm lack of response indicating full anesthesia.
Inject subcutaneously 1 mg/kg tramadol (or equivalent analgesic).
Shave the abdomen using a razor blade or an electric razor.
Disinfect the abdominal area with iodine solution followed by 70% ethanol.
Make a 5 mm incision along the alba line in the abdomen for skin and muscle layers to expose embryos.
Pull out the uterine horns carefully.
Expose embryos one by one and avoid twisting the uterus.
Keep the uterus moist with warm PBS (37°C) during surgery.
Draw a map of the exposed uterus, reproducing embryos in left and right horns.
Insert the glass capillary into the lateral ventricle of each brain carefully.
Inject approximately 1–2 μL of DNA mix solution.
Immerse electrodes in saline solution (PBS) to improve conductivity.
Hold the head of each embryo with a fine tweezer to position the electrodes on each side of the ventricles.
Match the positive (+) pole of the electrode with the side of the injection.
Run the electroporation using ΔV = 39 V, pulse time: 50 ms, number of pulses: 5, resting time between pulses: 950 ms, polarity: unipolar.
Return embryos to the abdominal cavity using tweezers.
Clean the area with 500 μL PBS pre-warmed at 37°C.
Suture the inner muscular layer of the mouse.
Suture the outer skin layer of the mouse.
Place the animal in a quiet place for recovery from anesthesia.
Monitor mouse recovery after surgery.
Sacrifice the mouse using a CO2 chamber followed by cervical dislocation two days post-surgery.
Remove and sacrifice embryos by decapitation if necessary.
Isolate brains and transfer to a petri dish containing pre-chilled PBS.
Check GFP-positive brains using a fluorescent/stereo microscope (10×–20× magnification).
Transfer GFP-brains to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Fix the brains in 4% v/v PFA overnight at 4°C with gentle agitation.
Place the fixed brains in a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube with 30% v/v sucrose solution and incubate at 4°C for 18–24 h.
Remove from sucrose and immerse brains in cryopreservant solution at -20°C until solid.
Using a cryostat, slice cerebral cortex into 40 μm coronal sections.
Transfer brain into gelatin pre-coated glass slides.
Permeabilize cortical slices with 0.3% v/v Triton X-100-PBS solution for 15 min at RT.
Incubate DAPI for 15 min at RT (20°C–25°C).
Make 3 washes of 5 min each with PBS at RT.
Seal samples using Mowiol.
Set up a wide-field microscope for imaging.
Perform z-stack imaging of GFP-positive cortices at the required magnification.
Take multiple fields if necessary to reconstruct the whole cortex during post-imaging.
Use Fiji software and go to "z-project" to project maximal intensity fluorescence.
Stitch images using the Fiji stitching plugin if needed to reconstruct the whole cortex.
Divide the cortex into four layers: ventricular zone, subventricular zone, intermediate zone, cortical plate.
Quantify the number of GFP-positive cells in each layer using the Fiji cell counter plugin.
Estimate the number of rounds, multipolar and bipolar cells in each layer by visual inspection and cell counting.
Note that neuronal polarization occurs in the IZ of the cortex where multipolar neurons acquire a bipolar morphology with leading and trailing neurites.
Use morphological parameters to discriminate between polarized (bipolar) and unpolarized neurons (multipolar or round cells).
Consider molecular markers such as LKB1, TAG-1, Trb1, Tbr2, MAP2, and SMI-312 to identify each phenotype during polarization of neurons in situ.
